## Summary

Add a hover tooltip to the persistent synergy lines drawn between adjacent
synergistic businesses on the Main Street board. Hovering a line explains the
shared synergy type and the per-turn effect that link has on each of the two
connected cards.

## User Story

As a Main Street player, I want to hover over a synergy line and see what that
synergy does — the shared type and the coins/reputation each linked business
gains from it — so that I can understand *why* two businesses are connected and
plan my street deliberately, instead of guessing from the line colour alone.

## Problem Statement

The board draws coloured synergy lines between adjacent businesses that share a
synergy type, but the lines are purely decorative: hovering them does nothing.
The player sees that two cards are linked but not which synergy type they share,
the rate that applies, or the value of that specific connection. The only
synergy information available today is the per-card `Synergy: <types>` line in
the business-slot tooltip, which does not explain the link or its magnitude.

## Existing State

- `drawSynergyLines()` in
  `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` draws a
  two-pass `Phaser.GameObjects.Graphics` line (core + glow) per synergy pair and
  adds it to `streetContainer`. The graphics objects are **not interactive** —
  there is no input handler on them.
- `computeSynergyPairs()` in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyNeighbors.ts`
  returns `SynergyPair { fromIndex, toIndex, sharedSynergy }`, the data the
  renderer iterates to draw each line. Sold cards still participate as pair
  endpoints (CG-0MT5XUE2200047IJ).
- Per-card synergy maths lives in
  `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`:
  `computeSynergyBonus()` (coin), `computeSynergyRepBonus()` (reputation),
  `effectiveSynergyCoinBonus()` / `effectiveSynergyRepBonus()`. The difficulty
  multiplier is `config.synergyBonusPerNeighbor`.
- Existing formatting helpers live in
  `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` (`effectiveSynergyRate()`,
  `formatSynergyRate()`, `formatPerTurnReputation()`, `formatCurrency()`).
- Business-slot tooltips already use the shared `TooltipManager`
  (`s.tooltipManager?.show(info, x, y)` / `.hide()`); the manager is created
  only when `!s.replayMode`
  (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`) and already honours the
  `settingsPanel.showTooltips` toggle.

## Desired Change

1. Add a pure, unit-testable content builder — e.g.
   `buildSynergyLinkTooltipInfo(grid, fromIndex, toIndex, sharedSynergy, config, soldSlots?, gridDims?)`
   in `MainStreetFormatting.ts` — that returns the tooltip text for one link.
2. In `drawSynergyLines()`, give each line a **narrow, invisible interactive hit
   area** (parented into `streetContainer`, drawn/recreated with the rest of the
   street layer) wired to `tooltipManager.show(...)` on `pointerover` and
   `tooltipManager.hide()` on `pointerout`.
3. Guard the wiring the same way existing slot tooltips are: no tooltip in
   `replayMode` and no tooltip when `tooltipManager` is absent; the
   `showTooltips` setting continues to be enforced by `TooltipManager` itself.
4. Ensure the hit area does not swallow the existing business-slot hover/click
   interactions except immediately along the line (see Constraints).

### Suggested tooltip format (implementation may refine wording)

```
Food synergy
Bakery  ⟷  Diner
Bakery: +2 coins/turn from this link
Diner: +1 coins/turn from this link
+5 reputation/turn  (only when a reputation-synergy contribution exists)
```

Sold endpoints are called out explicitly, e.g.
`Bakery (sold): earns nothing, but still anchors this synergy`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Hovering a persistent synergy line shows a tooltip that names the shared
  synergy type and states the per-turn coin and/or reputation effect of that
  link for **each** endpoint, computed with the active difficulty multiplier
  (`config.synergyBonusPerNeighbor`).
- The tooltip is hidden when the pointer leaves the line, and is not shown at
  all in replay mode; the existing `settingsPanel.showTooltips = false` toggle
  suppresses it (via `TooltipManager`).
- A sold endpoint is represented correctly: it earns nothing from the link
  itself, while the link still anchors synergy for the other endpoint, and the
  tooltip says so.
- The line hover hit area does not break the existing business-slot
  interactions: slot hover tooltips, click-to-place, sell, and upgrade
  targeting continue to work everywhere except the line's immediate vicinity.
- Unit tests cover the pure `buildSynergyLinkTooltipInfo()` builder (shared
  type, coin-only, reputation, sold endpoint, zero-synergy opt-out, difficulty
  multiplier) and an automated test covers the hover wiring on a rendered line.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Reuse the shared `TooltipManager` (`@ui`) — do **not** add a bespoke tooltip
  renderer, consistent with
  [Standardize TooltipManager across all games] (CG-0MPKE6W1C0047A44) and
  [Tooltip single-source fix] (CG-0MTJP6RNL008LGF3).
- Keep the content builder **pure** (no Phaser/scene dependency) so it can be
  unit-tested headless, mirroring `synergyLineEndpoints.ts`.
- Synergy lines are drawn **after** the slot rectangles in `drawSynergyLines()`,
  so their hit areas sit on top of the slot hit zones. The hit area must be
  narrow (a thin band around the segment, thick enough for a mouse but not so
  thick that it steals slot hover) and the chosen thickness/approach must be
  documented in a code comment.
- Hit areas are recreated on every `streetContainer` rebuild (the street layer
  is rebuilt by `refreshAll()`), so their creation must not leak listeners or
  leave stale objects behind.
- Reduced-motion: no animation is introduced; the tooltip appears/hides
  immediately, so reduced-motion preferences are unaffected.
- No new engine-level (`src/`) API is expected — Main Street-local formatting +
  renderer wiring only.
- Out of scope: tooltips on the transient synergy-formation animation line,
  changing the synergy formula, and changing line geometry/colours.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — Add an
  interactive hit area per synergy pair inside `drawSynergyLines()` and wire it
  to `s.tooltipManager`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — New pure
  `buildSynergyLinkTooltipInfo()` builder (shared synergy type + per-endpoint
  coin/reputation effect).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — Reuse/extract the
  per-link contribution maths if a per-neighbour share helper is needed
  (avoid duplicating the synergy formula).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyNeighbors.ts` — Source of
  `SynergyPair`; may need no change beyond typing.
- `tests/main-street/synergy-tooltip.test.ts` — New unit tests for the content
  builder.
- `tests/main-street/synergy-tooltip.browser.test.ts` — New browser test for
  hover wiring (or extend `tests/main-street/synergy-visuals.test.ts`).
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — Document the synergy-line tooltip
  interaction.
- `example-games/main-street/README.md` — Mention the tooltip in the synergy
  overview (if the README describes synergy lines).

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Assumption (documented, producer may adjust):** "the effect of that synergy"
  means the shared type plus the per-link per-turn coin/reputation contribution
  for each endpoint, rather than a generic rules paragraph. The suggested
  format above is a proposal; wording can change without altering the ACs.
- **Risk — per-link vs. card-total mismatch:** `computeSynergyBonus()` rounds
  the *total* across all matching neighbours, so a per-link share may not sum
  exactly to the displayed card total. The tooltip must not imply a precision
  it does not have; document the chosen presentation (per-link share formatted
  to at most one decimal, or card total) in the builder's doc comment.
- **Risk — input interception:** adding interactive objects on top of the slot
  hit zones can regress slot hover/click. Mitigation: narrow hit band + an
  explicit regression test for slot hover/click; keep the band culled with the
  line.
- **Risk — re-render churn:** `drawSynergyLines()` runs on every refresh; a
  fresh hit area per refresh must be destroyed with the container or it leaks.
- **Scope-creep guard:** any desire to also tooltip the *animated* formation
  line, restyle lines, or change synergy values must be filed as a separate
  work item, not folded into this one.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MM4REC2Z0GS2YKT** – Main Street: PRD Milestone 2 -- Full Content and Crafting/Building System (completed)
- **CG-0MQQHCJJ5009AB4X** – Fix Lighting Spike scene visibility (completed)
- **CG-0MQOBJ9BW006TTJR** – Main Street score tooltip should show calculation breakdown (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: effect, lines, provide, should, showing (+2 more)
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: effect, lines, provide, should, showing (+2 more)
- `example-games/gym/README.md` — matched: effect, lines, provide, should, showing (+2 more)

### Manual related references

- **CG-0MQQHBZ3D002J02E** – Add visual synergy lines between adjacent businesses
  (completed): introduced the lines this work item makes interactive.
- **CG-0MSVM3WCD007BRQP** – Synergy lines drawn edge-to-edge / corner-to-corner
  (completed): `synergyLineEndpoints.ts` geometry reused for the hit band.
- **CG-0MT5XUE2200047IJ** – Main Street sold businesses still provide synergy
  (completed): defines sold-endpoint semantics the tooltip must reflect.
- **CG-0MPKE6W1C0047A44** – Standardize TooltipManager across all games
  (completed): the shared tooltip component to reuse.
- **CG-0MTJP6RNL008LGF3** – Tooltip single-source fix (completed): tooltip
  content should come from shared formatters.
- **CG-0MT5Y9AD2001MKWZ** – Tooltips on businesses are confusing (completed):
  precedent for clarifying Main Street tooltip wording.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — synergy line visual/audio spec
  (lines, coin flights, animation) to extend with the tooltip.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was required: the seed context and the existing
Main Street code path (`drawSynergyLines` → `SynergyPair` → per-card synergy
formula → `TooltipManager`) were sufficient to draft a clear brief. The single
open design decision was resolved by documented assumption:

- **Assumption A1 (tooltip content):** the tooltip shows the shared synergy
  type and the per-link per-turn coin/reputation contribution for each
  endpoint, rather than a generic rules sentence. Rationale: this matches the
  wording "showing the effect of that synergy" and the precedent set by
  [Add scoring tooltip to expedition column headers] (CG-0MLXCSSES11VPL3C),
  which surfaces the live contribution rather than a definition. Source:
  repo evidence (`SynergyPair.sharedSynergy`, `computeSynergyBonus`,
  `computeSynergyRepBonus`). **OPEN QUESTION for the producer:** confirm the
  proposed format, or specify an alternative (e.g. show the card's *total*
  synergy bonus instead of the per-link share).

## Failure Signature

- Test name: ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts — Last Round card: flips on the deck, settles at the resting position, and is omitted from its slot (waitForCondition timed out)
- Failing commit: latest `dev` at triage (root cause commit `21688987`, CG-0MUDMU0L8005YYE4)
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
Failure screenshot: tests/coloretto/__screenshots__/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts/... omits from slot-1.png. check tests/coloretto/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts:94:22 — Error: waitForCondition timed out. Seen during a full-suite run under heavy concurrent-agent CPU contention (load 25-49 on 16 cores); passes 26/26 in isolation at the same commit. discovered-from:CG-0MU3VH7QW006A2XA
```

## Root Cause

Not CPU-contention flakiness. The test now fails deterministically (~4 of 5 isolated runs at current `dev`).

Commit `21688987` (CG-0MUDMU0L8005YYE4) added `wholeRowValue()` and extended the Coloretto heuristic AI take gate to `netRowValue >= TAKE_THRESHOLD OR wholeRowValue >= TAKE_THRESHOLD` (`TAKE_THRESHOLD = 2`). A single bonus card has `wholeRowValue = BONUS_POINTS = 2`, so the AI now takes any row containing a bonus card.

In this test the AI's first turn may place a bonus card on a row (the session RNG defaults to `Math.random`, so the shuffled deck — and therefore the AI's first-turn card — varies run to run). After the human draws the Last Round card, the AI's final turn is then a TAKE, not a PLACE. The take animation (`playTakeAnimation`) uses flyers and never sets `flightCard`, so the test's fourth `waitForCondition` (`phase === 'animating' && flightCard !== null`) can never be satisfied; the round ends and phase becomes `round-scoring`.

Full investigation and evidence are recorded in the Plan-investigation comment.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout current `dev`: `git checkout <commit-hash>`
2. Run the failing test:
   `npx vitest run --project browser tests/coloretto/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts -t "Last Round card"`
3. Repeat several times: the failure depends on whether the AI's first turn drew a bonus card.

## Impact

Blocks the Coloretto browser suite on `dev`. The AI change is intended behaviour; the test's assumption that the AI's final turn is a placement is the brittle part.

## Recommended Fix Direction

Make the test deterministic or action-agnostic, e.g.:

- Control `scene.session.rows` before the human's placement so the AI has no row worth taking (forces a place, preserving the existing flight-card assertions); and/or
- Treat the AI's final turn as either place or take and wait on the round transition rather than `flightCard`.

## Key Files

- `tests/coloretto/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts`
- `example-games/coloretto/ColorettoAis.ts`
- `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoRenderer.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts — Last Round card: flips on the deck, settles at the resting position, and is omitted from its slot` passes reliably against the latest `dev` (e.g. 10 consecutive isolated runs, plus a normal suite run), with the AI's final turn either a place or a take.
2. The test no longer depends on the AI's strategy choice or on a specific shuffled deck (no new flakiness under CPU contention).
3. Documentation is updated only if the fix changes documented behaviour; a test-only fix requires no doc change.
4. The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun the test locally several times.
2. Root cause is known (see above); route to implementation.

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- Root-cause investigation: Plan-investigation comment on this work item
- Related: CG-0MUDMU0L8005YYE4 (AI `wholeRowValue` take-gate change)
- CI artifacts: (not available)

# `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` is not self-contained: fails under a bare unit run

**discovered-from:CG-0MUIMM28K001W88F** (found while triaging the `npm --silent test` test-failure item)

## Problem statement

`tests/golf/replay.test.ts` invokes the replay CLI as a subprocess
(`node --import tsx/esm scripts/replay.ts`) and inherits the ambient
environment. The CLI registers replay adapters from the active preset
(`configs/<preset>.json`, selected by `GAMES_CONFIG`), and its default preset
is `core-only` — which contains no games, so no adapters are registered. The
golf adapter is only loaded when `GAMES_CONFIG` resolves to a preset that
includes golf (`solo`, `arcade`, `full`).

`scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` exports `GAMES_CONFIG="${GAMES_CONFIG:-full}"` before
its stages, so the test passes in the CI/full-suite path. Any *bare* targeted or
whole-profile unit run, however, uses the default `core-only` preset and the
file fails with four assertion failures:

```
Error: Could not auto-detect game type from transcript.
Available adapters: none. Use --game <type> to specify explicitly.
```

Failing assertions observed locally at `dev` HEAD `933644bc`
(`npx vitest run --project unit tests/golf/replay.test.ts`):
- `Tests  4 failed | 21 passed | 5 skipped (30)`
- `Test Files  1 failed | 2 passed (3)` when run alongside the two new main-street tests.

This contradicts the project's documented workflow, which tells developers and
agents to run the unit profile directly (`npx vitest run --project unit ...`,
`npm test -- --project unit`; see `AGENTS.md` → *Running Test Profiles* and
*When to run which tests*). A developer following that guidance sees a red unit
profile for reasons unrelated to their change, and a whole-profile
`npx vitest run --project unit` is currently red on a clean `dev` checkout.

Evidence (local, 2026-09-26):

| Command | `GAMES_CONFIG` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `npx vitest run --project unit tests/golf/replay.test.ts` | unset (→ `core-only`) | **4 failed**, 1 failed file; `Could not auto-detect game type ... Available adapters: none.` |
| `GAMES_CONFIG=full npx vitest run --project unit tests/golf/replay.test.ts` | `full` | 16 passed, 5 skipped |
| `GAMES_CONFIG=full npx tsx scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts --project unit` (whole profile) | `full` | 418 files passed, 7173 passed / 8 skipped — green |

The file's fixture path was also touched in the failing commit (`a341ec3c`,
"Incidental unblock: `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` fixture path corrected to the
launcher checkout layout"), so the fixture path itself is now correct and is
not the cause.

## Users

- **Developer / agent running the documented minimum test bar (primary):** needs
  `npx vitest run --project unit` to be green on a clean checkout without
  knowing which preset the target test implicitly depends on.
- **Maintainer (secondary):** needs tests to declare their own preconditions so
  preset/environment coupling is explicit rather than an ambient accident.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **The unit profile is green without environment priming:** `npx vitest run --project unit tests/golf/replay.test.ts` passes on a clean `dev` checkout with `GAMES_CONFIG` unset (and with `GAMES_CONFIG=core-only`). *Verified by:* the command exiting 0 and reporting no failed tests.
2. **The test declares its own preset:** the file arranges the preset it needs (e.g. sets `GAMES_CONFIG` explicitly in the subprocess environment for the adapter-dependent cases, or points `--game golf` at the adapter it requires) instead of relying on an ambient export from a shell wrapper. The chosen mechanism is documented in a code comment explaining why the CLI needs an adapter-registering preset.
3. **Adapter-dependent cases still exercise the real CLI path:** the tests that assert replay/validation behaviour against the golf fixture still run the real `scripts/replay.ts` subprocess with the golf adapter registered — they are not weakened into unit-level mocks or `it.skip`.
4. **No regression to the CI/full path:** `GAMES_CONFIG=full npx tsx scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts --project unit` remains green, and `tests/scripts/distribution-presets.test.ts` / `tests/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.test.ts` (which assert the `core-only` default and the shell runners' `GAMES_CONFIG=full` default) are unchanged or updated consistently.
5. **Sibling coupling audited:** any other test file with the same latent dependency on an ambient adapter-registering preset is identified and either fixed the same way or recorded. *Verified by:* grepping `tests/` for subprocess invocations of `scripts/replay.ts` (or other adapter-consuming CLIs) and confirming each sets its own preset.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments and the troubleshooting notes in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` if a new convention is introduced.
7. **Full project test suite passes with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Do not weaken the tests to make them pass.** Skipping or mocking the adapter-dependent cases is not an acceptable fix; the run must remain a real CLI integration check.
- **Do not change the `core-only` default.** `core-only` is the deliberate production default (`GAMES_CONFIG` unset) and is asserted by existing tests; the fix belongs in the test, not the default preset.
- Keep changes surgical: this item covers test hermeticity only; the `[vitest-worker]` transient-contention failure is CG-0MUIMM28K001W88F.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` — the subprocess helper's environment (`runReplay`'s `env: { ...process.env }`) and the `FIXTURE_TRANSCRIPT` constant.
- `scripts/replay.ts` — adapter registration from the selected preset (`registerConfiguredAdapters(process.cwd())`).
- `scripts/adapters/index.ts` — `registerConfiguredAdapters` candidate-path resolution.
- `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` — `selectConfigPath` / `DEFAULT_PRESET = 'core-only'`.
- `configs/solo.json`, `configs/full.json` — presets that include golf.
- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` — the `export GAMES_CONFIG="${GAMES_CONFIG:-full}"` that masks the defect in CI.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — CPU-contention / test-profile documentation to extend if a convention is introduced.

## Related work

- **CG-0MUIMM28K001W88F** — the `[test-failure]` item this was discovered from (transient Vitest worker RPC timeout defeating the retry guard).
- **CG-0MTW1EN0D003CSA0** — `validate all card text`; its commit `a341ec3c` carried the "incidental unblock" that corrected this file's fixture path and is the commit the reported failure was observed at.
- **CG-0MUILDS3200656TU** — referenced by that commit for the fixture-path correction.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: the fix hides a real preset-coupling bug (low).** The CLI's default preset is deliberately `core-only`; the test's need for an adapter is a *test* precondition, so setting it in the test is correct. *Mitigation:* AC2 requires a code comment stating why.
- **Risk: `GAMES_CONFIG` set per-subprocess diverges from the CI path (low).** *Mitigation:* AC4 requires the full-preset run to stay green.
- **Assumption:** the only preset-dependent surface in this file is the subprocess environment (the fixture path and the summary-report assertions are preset-independent).
- **Assumption:** other example-game replay tests, if any, are preset-independent or already covered by AC5's audit.

## Context

# Add per-turn running costs to Playground, Town Fountain and Community Shelter

## Summary

Give the three remaining free-to-run Main Street community-space cards a per-turn running cost, following the Park precedent (CG-0MU9NW9EP003B1AK) and the producer decision of 2026-09-29. Today the Playground (`cs-playground`), Town Fountain (`cs-fountain`) and Community Shelter (`cs-shelter`) have `ongoingCost` empty → 0, so they are free synergy/reputation anchors.

## Problem statement

The Park was given a 40 coins/turn running cost to stop costless synergy spam. Three other community spaces still have no ongoing cost, so the same "free anchor" dynamic remains for their synergies:

- **Playground** (`cs-playground`) — cost 400, Entertainment, +5 rep/turn, ongoing 0.
- **Town Fountain** (`cs-fountain`) — cost 500, Culture, +10 rep/turn, ongoing 0.
- **Community Shelter** (`cs-shelter`) — cost 600, Service, +15 rep/turn, ongoing 0 (retiered T6→T3, CG-0MT5VZJLS000B8KI).

## Users

- **Player** — building a Playground/Fountain/Shelter cluster should feel the per-turn drain as a real strategic cost.
- **Producer / balance owner** — wants a running-cost lever on every community space, not just Park/Library/Garden/Kiosk/Public Art.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Card data** — `cs-playground`, `cs-fountain` and `cs-shelter` in the Main Street `card-data.csv` each have a non-zero integer `ongoingCost`, confirmed with the producer before merge. **Proposed mapping (agent suggestion, producer-owned — confirm or override): Playground 20, Town Fountain 25, Community Shelter 30.**
2. **Descriptions** — each updated `card-data.csv` description states the running cost using the existing wording ("Costs N coins per turn to run."), consistent with Library/Community Garden/Park, and the `card-text-data-consistency` test passes.
3. **Deduction** — at end of turn each placed, unsold card deducts its `ongoingCost` through the existing `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts()` path, clamped at 0 coins and logged with an insufficient-funds log when applicable.
4. **Tooltips** — each card's community-space tooltip shows `Ongoing cost: -N/turn`; each card's cash line shows `-N`.
5. **Sold-card exemption preserved** — a sold Playground/Fountain/Shelter incurs no ongoing cost (CG-0MU3VH7QW006A2XA).
6. **Tests** — add distinct coverage for each card's deduction, clamping and sold-exemption (no redundant duplicates); update any test that assumes these cards are free to run (e.g. `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` "does not deduct for zero-ongoing-cost cards" currently uses Playground + Fountain + Shelter and must be re-pointed at cards that remain free, or reworked).
7. **Balance sanity** — Monte Carlo and tutorial guardrails remain green; any drift is measured and reported, and no guardrail band is silently widened. Note the tutorial scenario places no Playground/Fountain/Shelter (verify).
8. **Docs** — update `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` (Ongoing/turn column), `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`, `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` (special-cases) and any other doc listing these cards' running costs.
9. **Full project test suite passes.**

## Constraints

- **Integer economy (hard):** coins are whole integers (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6); no fractional `ongoingCost`.
- **Data is source of truth:** the running cost lives in `card-data.csv`; tooltip, overlay and deduction derive from it.
- **Charging semantics unchanged:** placed, unsold cards only; clamped at 0; reuse the existing community-space mechanism.
- **Balance values are producer-owned:** the proposed mapping is an agent suggestion; the producer confirms or overrides before merge.

## Existing state

- `cs-playground`: cost 400, baseIncome 0, Entertainment, rep 5, `ongoingCost` empty.
- `cs-fountain`: cost 500, baseIncome 0, Culture, rep 10, `ongoingCost` empty.
- `cs-shelter`: cost 600, baseIncome 0, Service, rep 15, `ongoingCost` empty.
- Park precedent: `docs/main-street/...`; commit `5ffd54a` in `tce-main-street` set `cs-park` to 40/turn and updated tests/tooltip/cash-line/docs.
- Test that assumes they are free: `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` "does not deduct for zero-ongoing-cost cards".

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` (tce-main-street repo) — set the three `ongoingCost` values and descriptions.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` — regenerated by the suite; no SVG face change expected (community-space ongoing cost is not baked in).
- `tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` — add per-card deduction/clamp/sold coverage.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-tooltip.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/ongoing-cost-tooltips.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` — tooltip/cash-line coverage.
- `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` — rework the zero-cost test.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md`, `card-catalog.md`, `balancing-methodology.md`.

## Related work

- **CG-0MU9NW9EP003B1AK** — Park running cost 40/turn (precedent; producer confirmed the integer-economy mapping).
- CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6 — integer economy ×100 rescale.
- CG-0MU3VH7QW006A2XA — sold cards excluded from ongoing costs.
- CG-0MRXYGM9B006I3PE — community-space ongoing-cost / Park-model synergy.
- CG-0MSQJ210I00491ZZ — Group B community-space expansion (added these three cards).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Value assumption:** the three proposed values (20/25/30) are an agent suggestion; the producer must confirm or override before merge.
- **Balance drift:** these cards appear in Monte Carlo simulations; run the guardrails and report drift rather than widening bands.
- **Test coupling:** the existing "does not deduct for zero-ongoing-cost cards" test uses exactly these three cards, so it must be updated (this is expected, not a regression).
